uncited: *   **Input:** SBRT dataset (grid dimensions $grid_{ancho} \times grid_{alto}$, maximum intervals $m$), camera parameters, light source position, Transfer Function (discrete lookup table), and rendering resolution.
The volumetric data is encoded into one or two GPU structures (textures or buffers).
The specific layout depends on the chosen memory approach (see Subtopics).
*   **Index Structure:** Maps 2D grid coordinates to stack start positions and sizes.
*   **Interval Structure:** Stores material attributes and accumulated heights for each interval.
*   **Transfer Function:** Discrete lookup table mapping material values to colors.
Uses an Index Texture ($grid_{ancho} \times grid_{alto}$) storing stack start (R) and size (G), and an Interval Texture storing material (R) and accumulated height (G).
Stacks are stored row-order in the Interval Texture.
*Sets apart:* Simple indexing but wastes memory in the last row.
*Choose when:* Memory is not a critical constraint and simplicity is preferred.
*Link:* [GPU Raycasting for Stack-Based Terrains](14281-gpu-ray-casting-pipeline.md)
Uses a single 2D Texture with dimensions $grid_{ancho} * \lceil \sqrt{m} \rceil \times grid_{alto} * \lceil \sqrt{m} \rceil$.
Regions of size $\lceil \sqrt{m} \rceil \times \lceil \sqrt{m} \rceil$ act as super-texels.
*Sets apart:* Pseudo-indexing via regions.
*Choose when:* $m$ is small and square regions are efficient.
*Link:* [GPU Raycasting for Stack-Based Terrains](14281-gpu-ray-casting-pipeline.md)
Uses a 2D Texture of dimensions $(grid_{ancho} * m) \times grid_{alto}$.
*Sets apart:* Checks spatial coherence against 3D textures.
*Choose when:* Spatial coherence is a priority.
*Link:* [GPU Raycasting for Stack-Based Terrains](14281-gpu-ray-casting-pipeline.md)
Uses a 3D Texture of dimensions $grid_{ancho} \times grid_{alto} \times m$.
*Sets apart:* Standard 3D texture access.
*Choose when:* 3D texture hardware is efficient.
*Link:* [GPU Raycasting for Stack-Based Terrains](14281-gpu-ray-casting-pipeline.md)
Uses two Shader Storage Buffer Objects (SSBOs) for indices and intervals, using OpenGL std430 layout.
*Sets apart:* Flexible array sizes, large memory support (128 MB min).
*Choose when:* Large datasets or dynamic stack sizes.
*Link:* [GPU Raycasting for Stack-Based Terrains](14281-gpu-ray-casting-pipeline.md)
